events.name: Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix 2026 (first SG Sprint weekend)
events.attendees: ~270,000 three-day attendance, roughly half international
events.rationale: Re-confirmed this run: 9-11 October 2026 at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, and the Sprint format is confirmed as Singapore's first, with Sprint qualifying on Friday and the Sprint race on Saturday, making Friday a full ticketed race day rather than a practice day. NEW DETAIL THIS RUN: the full entertainment line-up has been released - JJ Lin and CORTIS on Friday, Zara Larsson and The Killers on Saturday, James Arthur and Lana Del Rey on Sunday, across ten stages including the Padang. The Sprint plus a stronger music bill both lengthen the average stay: historic F1 weeks already run 4-6 nights for international fans, and the Friday Sprint pulls arrivals forward to Wednesday/Thursday. Attendee mix is overwhelmingly adult, high-spend and fly-in (Australia, UK, Japan, Indonesia, Malaysia, India, Middle East), which is the single best-matched profile for an adults-only CBD aparthotel. This is also the peak compression week of the entire horizon: TOKEN2049 (7-8 Oct), the Milken Institute Asia Summit (7-9 Oct), Hans Zimmer at the Indoor Stadium (7 Oct) and the AFTER 2049 closing party (9 Oct) all bleed directly into the race weekend, so citywide compression starts around 5 October and does not release until 12 October. Price for a minimum-stay race-week block, not for individual nights.
events.best_fit: The Quays and City Hall. Both sit inside or immediately beside the circuit footprint - City Hall properties are walking distance to the Padang and Zone 4 gates, and The Quays give guests a walkable route back along the river after 1am concert finishes when road closures make taxis unusable. Chinatown works as spillover via Telok Ayer/Tanjong Pagar.

events.name: TOKEN2049 Singapore
events.attendees: 25,000+ delegates, 7,000+ companies, 500+ exhibitors, 300+ speakers
events.rationale: Dates re-confirmed this run on the official site: 7-8 October 2026, taking over all five floors of Marina Bay Sands, with the AFTER 2049 closing party on 9 October at the SkyPark Observation Deck. Headline number has grown to 25,000+ expected attendees. This is the strongest single demand event of the horizon after F1 on a per-room basis: attendees are almost entirely adult, international (Europe, US, Middle East, Greater China, Korea), and the crypto crowd books late, pays high and stays 4-6 nights because of the enormous unofficial side-event programme that runs across Clarke Quay, Tanjong Pagar and Amoy Street for a full week either side. The 9 October closing party deliberately dovetails into F1 Friday, so a large share of TOKEN2049 delegates extend through the race weekend rather than departing - treat 5-12 October as one continuous sold-out block. Overlaps this run also include the Milken Institute Asia Summit (7-9 Oct, NEW) and Hans Zimmer at the Indoor Stadium (7 Oct, NEW), tightening the same nights further.
events.best_fit: The Quays and Chinatown. The Quays are the epicentre of TOKEN2049 side events and after-parties along the river, and Chinatown/Telok Ayer hosts the bulk of the crypto-fund and VC satellite events - both are 10-15 minutes to Bayfront. City Hall is a solid third for direct MBS access.

events.name: SuperReturn Asia 2026
events.attendees: 2,500+ private markets professionals, 1,200+ LPs and 1,000+ GPs from 50+ countries
events.rationale: Dates and venue re-confirmed this run: 28 September to 1 October 2026 at Marina Bay Sands. Attendee profile is close to ideal - senior, adult, corporate-funded, from 50+ countries, with a heavy North American and European fly-in contingent that typically arrives the weekend before and stays 4-5 nights. Length of stay is extended further by the informal 'SuperReturn Asia Week' satellite programme of LP dinners and GP roadshows that runs around the main conference. The critical planning point this run is the overlap stack: SuperReturn's tail (30 Sep-1 Oct) runs straight into Tech Week Singapore (29-30 Sep), then The Weeknd's two National Stadium nights (2-3 Oct) and ITZY (3 Oct), so the 28 September to 3 October block should be treated as continuously compressed with no soft midweek. Corporate rate ceilings are high and this segment is not price-sensitive.
events.best_fit: City Hall and The Quays. City Hall gives the shortest walk/Circle Line hop to Bayfront for early-morning plenaries, while The Quays suit the evening LP-dinner circuit around Boat Quay and Robertson Quay. Chinatown works for delegates who also want Telok Ayer/Amoy Street dining.

events.name: Tech Week Singapore 2026
events.attendees: 29,000+ attendees, 500+ exhibitors, 500+ international speakers
events.rationale: Dates re-confirmed this run on the official site: 29-30 September 2026 at Sands Expo. Headline attendance is now stated at 29,000+, consolidating five co-located shows (Cloud and AI Infrastructure Asia, DevOps Live!, Cyber Security World Asia, Data Centre World Asia, Big Data and AI World Asia). Materialisation history is strong - this show has grown every edition and delivers reliably. The caveat that keeps it at High rather than Very High is mix: a meaningful share of the 29,000 are Singapore-based day-attendees who do not book rooms. The room-generating cohort is the exhibitor and speaker base plus regional delegates from India, Australia, Japan, Korea and ASEAN, who typically book 3-4 nights with a Monday-in/Thursday-out shape. Its value this run is compression rather than absolute volume: it sits directly on top of SuperReturn Asia (28 Sep-1 Oct) and immediately before The Weeknd (2-3 Oct), so the last week of September has no soft night.
events.best_fit: City Hall and The Quays for direct Bayfront/Marina Bay access to Sands Expo; Chinatown as the value alternative for exhibitor teams and smaller vendors who are more rate-sensitive but still want a CBD address.

events.name: F✦FOREVER 1st World Tour in Singapore
events.attendees: ~12,000 per night across three nights (~36,000 total)
events.rationale: Re-confirmed this run on Live Nation Singapore as a three-night run, 14-16 August 2026, doors 6.30pm and show 8pm - no cancellation, no date change, and no added or dropped night with nine days to go. Line-up is F4 (Jerry Yan, Van Ness Wu, Vic Chou) with Mayday's Ashin, and Singapore is the final Southeast Asian leg, which historically pulls a strong cross-border fly-in from Malaysia, Indonesia, Taiwan, Hong Kong and mainland China. The audience is squarely adult Mandopop nostalgia demographic - 35-55, couples and friend groups, no children - which is an excellent fit for an adults-only product. Three consecutive nights at 12,000 capacity is a large room block by any measure, and multi-night ticket holders extend to 3-4 nights. It also lands immediately after the National Day long weekend (8-10 Aug), so mid-August should be held firm rather than discounted.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam first - it is the closest of the four sectors to the Kallang precinct, one or two stops on the Circle/Downtown lines via Nicoll Highway or Lavender, and the late-night walk/short-ride home after an 11pm finish is the deciding factor for this audience. City Hall is the strong second via Stadium/Mountbatten.

events.name: Franchising & Licensing Asia 2026 (FLAsia)
events.attendees: 7,000+ business leaders, investors and decision-makers; 150+ exhibitors, 250+ brands
events.rationale: Dates re-confirmed this run: 13-15 August 2026 at Sands Expo, 21st edition, now organised by MP Singapore. Expected 7,000+ business leaders, investors, entrepreneurs and decision-makers over three days, with country pavilions from Australia, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Spain, Thailand, the UK and Vietnam, plus exhibitors from Hong Kong, Malaysia, the Philippines and Taiwan. That pavilion structure is what drives the demand call - national delegations book as blocks, arrive a day early for set-up, and stay the full three days, so the fly-in share and length of stay are both well above a typical trade show. Attendees are adult B2B buyers and franchisees with company-paid budgets. It sits inside the same eight-day August cluster as F✦FOREVER (14-16 Aug) at the Indoor Stadium and the Asian Actuarial Conference (18-21 Aug), which makes 13-21 August the strongest sustained stretch of the month.
events.best_fit: City Hall and The Quays for the short hop to Bayfront and Sands Expo. Chinatown is a good third for the Asian franchisee delegations, who tend to prefer Chinatown/Tanjong Pagar for dining and are more rate-conscious than the Western pavilions.

events.name: Post Malone - The BIG ASS Stadium World Tour
events.attendees: Up to 55,000
events.rationale: Re-confirmed this run: single night, Friday 25 September 2026 at the National Stadium, with Don Toliver as special guest - no second night added and no postponement. This is Post Malone's first full-length headline show in Singapore, which is exactly the profile that generates regional fly-in rather than purely local attendance: Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines and Australia all feed a Singapore-only SEA date. A Friday show is the best possible shape for the hotel - it converts naturally into a two- or three-night weekend stay rather than a single night. Audience skews adult 20-40, groups and couples. It also opens the compressed final week of September, running directly into SuperReturn Asia (28 Sep-1 Oct) and Tech Week (29-30 Sep), so the 25 September to 3 October stretch should be managed as one block with minimum-stay controls on the Friday.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam is the clear first choice for Kallang - Lavender/Nicoll Highway are one to two stops from Stadium and the post-show crowd exit is manageable on foot or by short ride. City Hall second; The Quays and Chinatown are viable but add a transfer for a 55,000-capacity egress.

events.name: BIGBANG 20th Anniversary World Tour <XX : COSMOS>
events.attendees: Up to 55,000
events.rationale: RESOLVED THIS RUN - the flag on the previous list is cleared. The show is now fully confirmed and publicly listed by Ticketmaster Singapore and The Kallang for Saturday 17 October 2026 at the National Stadium, 7pm, with the full nine-tier price ladder published (S$158 to S$498) and the V.I.P membership presale set for 11 August 2026. G-DRAGON, TAEYANG and DAESUNG are reuniting for a 17-city, 33-show stadium tour, their first together in nine years. That combination - stadium scale, 20th-anniversary framing, and a nine-year gap - produces the heaviest K-pop fly-in profile of the horizon, drawing from Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, Australia and Japan; the adult BIGBANG fanbase is now largely 28-40, travelling as couples and friend groups, which suits an adults-only product far better than a younger fourth-generation K-pop crowd. A Saturday date means Friday and Saturday nights both sell. Note the wider October compression: it lands the weekend after F1 (9-11 Oct) and the day before NCT 127 (18 Oct, NEW), so mid-October has no genuine trough. Watch the 11 August presale for a possible second night.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam first for Kallang proximity and late-night egress, then City Hall. The regional K-pop fly-in segment also indexes heavily on Bugis/Kampong Glam for shopping and late-night food, which reinforces the same call.

events.name: The Weeknd - After Hours Til Dawn Tour
events.attendees: Up to 55,000 per night across two nights
events.rationale: Re-confirmed this run on Live Nation Singapore: both nights hold, Friday 2 and Saturday 3 October 2026 at the National Stadium, doors 6pm, show 8pm, with Creepy Nuts and DJ ¥ØU$UK€ ¥UK1MAT$U supporting. Two consecutive stadium nights at 55,000 is the largest raw concert capacity in the entire horizon - roughly 110,000 admissions - and this is his first Singapore appearance since 2018 and the only Southeast Asian stop, so the regional fly-in share is unusually high for a Western pop act. Friday-Saturday shape is optimal: it converts to two- and three-night stays and lets guests bridge from the SuperReturn Asia/Tech Week corporate block that ends 1 October straight into the leisure weekend, with no changeover gap. ITZY at the Indoor Stadium on 3 October adds a further 12,000 on the Saturday. Hold firm, apply a two-night minimum on the Friday.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam for Kallang proximity and post-show egress, City Hall second. Given the size of the two-night draw, The Quays and Chinatown will also fill on overflow, but price them behind the two Kallang-adjacent sectors.

events.name: ITB Asia 2026
events.attendees: ~13,000-15,000 travel trade professionals from 130+ countries
events.rationale: Dates and venue re-confirmed this run against the official Event-At-A-Glance: 21-23 October 2026 at Marina Bay Sands, 09:30-18:00 daily, organised by Messe Berlin Asia Pacific. Asia's largest B2B travel trade show and about as pure a fly-in event as exists - buyers, sellers, tour operators, DMCs, NTOs and hospitality executives from well over a hundred countries, with essentially no local day-attendee dilution. Delegates are adult, corporate-funded, and stay 4-5 nights because of the appointment-based hosted-buyer format plus the dense evening networking programme. There is a second-order benefit worth noting: ITB delegates are themselves travel-trade decision-makers, so occupancy here has a distribution value beyond the room revenue. It follows a week behind BIGBANG (17 Oct) and NCT 127 (18 Oct) and runs directly into SIEW (26-30 Oct), making the second half of October nearly continuously occupied.
events.best_fit: City Hall and The Quays for the direct run to Bayfront and MBS. City Hall in particular suits the early-start hosted-buyer schedule. Chinatown is a credible third given Tanjong Pagar's F&B density for evening trade dinners.

events.name: Singapore International Energy Week (SIEW) 2026
events.venue: Marina Bay Sands / Sands Expo & Convention Centre
events.attendees: 15,000+ participants from 100+ countries
events.rationale: Re-confirmed this run via the Energy Market Authority: the 19th edition runs 26-30 October 2026 at Marina Bay Sands, themed 'Connecting Energy Systems, Powering Tomorrow', with 15,000+ participants expected from over 100 countries. Five days is the longest single-event footprint in the horizon, and the mix - ministers, utility and oil-and-gas executives, regulators, investors and technology suppliers - is senior, adult and almost entirely international, with corporate and government travel budgets that are insensitive to rate. Length of stay is genuinely five to six nights because the week is built from multiple co-located summits and roundtables rather than one conference. It overlaps the 17th IHPBA World Congress at Suntec (28-31 Oct) and follows ITB Asia (21-23 Oct), so the final third of October should be held at peak pricing with no last-minute discounting.
events.best_fit: City Hall and The Quays for Marina Bay proximity. City Hall is the primary call given the number of delegates who also have meetings in the Suntec/Raffles Place government and corporate corridor during the same week.

events.name: Milken Institute Asia Summit 2026
events.attendees: 1,500+ C-suite executives, global investors, policymakers and philanthropists
events.rationale: NEW THIS RUN - this was missing from the previous list and is a material omission. The Milken Institute's 2026 Asia Summit runs 7-9 October 2026 at the Four Seasons Hotel Singapore under the theme 'Leading with Intelligence', gathering 1,500+ C-suite executives, business leaders, global investors, policymakers and innovators. Headcount is modest but the demand quality is exceptional: this is the highest-net-worth adult delegate pool of the entire horizon, almost entirely fly-in from the US, Europe, the Gulf and North Asia, travelling with staff and typically staying four to six nights around the summit. Critically, it sits exactly on top of TOKEN2049 (7-8 Oct), the AFTER 2049 party (9 Oct), Hans Zimmer at the Indoor Stadium (7 Oct) and F1 practice/Sprint qualifying starting 9 October. The Four Seasons and the Orchard luxury cluster will be fully absorbed by the summit's own room block, which pushes overflow - executive assistants, junior staff, delegation support, media - into CBD product. Expect this event to be the reason a handful of otherwise-unexplained high-rate CBD bookings appear in the 5-10 October window.
events.best_fit: City Hall - it is the only one of the four sectors with a direct North-South Line run to Orchard for the Four Seasons, making it the natural overflow sector. The Quays second, since the summit's evening receptions and the concurrent TOKEN2049 side-event circuit both centre on the river.

events.name: MRO Asia-Pacific 2026
events.attendees: 7,500+ attendees, 350+ exhibitors from airlines, MROs, OEMs and lessors
events.rationale: NEW THIS RUN - previously missing from the list and confirmed on both the Aviation Week official site and the Singapore EXPO events calendar for 22-24 September 2026. It is the largest aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul event in Asia, drawing 7,500+ attendees and 350+ exhibitors from airlines, lessors, MROs, OEMs and suppliers across the global aviation supply chain. Attendee profile is exactly the target: senior, adult, technical and commercial aviation professionals with corporate travel budgets, overwhelmingly fly-in (there is no meaningful local day-attendee base for a global MRO show), and typically staying three to four nights for the combined senior conference and two-day exhibition. Venue is Singapore EXPO rather than the CBD, which is why it is High rather than Very High - some delegates default to Changi-side hotels - but aviation delegates consistently choose central Singapore for the evening programme, and the Downtown Line makes the EXPO commute straightforward. It also butts directly against Submarine Networks World (23-24 Sep) and the Singapore Tennis Open (21-27 Sep), reinforcing the same week.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam first - Bugis gives a direct Downtown Line ride to Expo with no interchange, which is the single biggest practical differentiator for an EXPO-based event. City Hall second via the East-West Line from City Hall/Bugis.

events.name: My Chemical Romance - The Black Parade World Tour
events.attendees: ~12,000 per night across two nights (~24,000 total)
events.rationale: Re-confirmed this run and both nights hold: 10 and 11 November 2026 at the Singapore Indoor Stadium, with the second night added on 11 November due to demand. Important history to keep visible - these shows were originally scheduled for 28 April 2026 and were postponed as part of a coordinated Southeast Asia rescheduling, with existing tickets rolled over and refunds offered. The postponement has already been absorbed and there is no sign of a further move, but it is worth a re-check closer in. Retained despite sitting just past the three-month edge because it materially shapes the booking horizon: it is the first Southeast Asian stop of the tour, so the regional fly-in share from Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand is high, and the audience is now a 30-45 adult nostalgia demographic that books early and stays two to three nights. Combined with LANY on 4 November, it means early-to-mid November is already firming and should not be opened at soft rates just because it is past the F1/SIEW peak.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam for Kallang proximity and late-night egress, City Hall second. The two-night structure means guests will look for a single continuous stay rather than moving, so lead with a two-night package in Kampong Glam.

events.name: National Day 2026 (NDP) + long weekend
events.attendees: ~55,000 at NDP plus citywide crowds
events.rationale: Re-confirmed this run through The Kallang's operational notices - NDP road closures and carpark closures around the Kallang precinct on 1 August (preview) and an NDP period Wi-Fi suspension inside the National Stadium running 21 July to 9 August, which places the 2026 parade at the National Stadium. National Day falls on Sunday 9 August 2026 with Monday 10 August as the public holiday, giving a three-day long weekend. Demand call stays at Medium and no higher, because the attendee mix is the weakest of any large event here: NDP tickets go to Singapore residents by ballot, the crowd is local and heavily family-oriented, and there is essentially no international overnight component. What does drive rooms is the regional short-haul leisure weekend - Malaysian, Indonesian and Filipino couples treating the long weekend as a city break - plus a staycation segment that an adults-only product only partially captures. Treat it as a solid but not premium three-night block, and note it runs straight into FLAsia (13-15 Aug) and F✦FOREVER (14-16 Aug), so there is no need to discount into mid-August afterwards.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam and City Hall. Kampong Glam is closest to the Kallang parade site and to the Marina Bay fireworks vantage points via Nicoll Highway; City Hall puts guests on the Padang/Marina Bay celebration circuit on foot.

events.name: Hans Zimmer Live - The Next Level
events.rationale: NEW THIS RUN - not on the previous list, confirmed for Wednesday 7 October 2026 at the Singapore Indoor Stadium, doors 5.30pm and show 7pm, presented by AEG Presents Asia, Semmel Concerts and RCI Global, with tickets S$148-S$468. It is Zimmer's first Singapore show since 2019, part of an Asia-Australia run also taking in Yokohama, Taipei, Kaohsiung, Beijing, Hangzhou, Chengdu and Guangzhou. Demand is Medium rather than High because a 12,000-seat midweek show draws a substantial local component, but two things elevate it above a routine concert. First, the audience is distinctly adult, affluent and couple-oriented - film-score and orchestral audiences skew 35-60 with high disposable income, which is a strong match for an adults-only aparthotel. Second, and more importantly for pricing, the date is the worst possible night to have spare inventory: 7 October is simultaneously day one of TOKEN2049, day one of the Milken Institute Asia Summit, and two days before F1 track action begins. Its practical effect is to remove the last soft midweek rooms in that week rather than to create a standalone block.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam for Kallang proximity on a 7pm midweek start where guests want the shortest possible commute after work-hours arrival. City Hall second - and note that many attendees that week are in town for TOKEN2049 or Milken and are already booked in City Hall or The Quays.

events.name: NCT 127 5TH TOUR 'NEO CITY - THE REDLINE'
events.rationale: NEW THIS RUN - not on the previous list, confirmed for Sunday 18 October 2026 at the Singapore Indoor Stadium as part of the fifth NCT 127 tour, which also stops in Jakarta, Hong Kong, Bangkok, Taipei, Manila, Kuala Lumpur, Saitama and Macau. The tour marks the return of most members from military service and supports a seventh full-length album released 24 August 2026. Demand is Medium: a 12,000-seat K-pop show generates real regional fly-in from Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and the Philippines, but because the tour also plays those markets directly, the cross-border share is lower than for a Singapore-exclusive date, and the fanbase skews younger than the BIGBANG or F✦FOREVER audiences, which is a weaker fit for an adults-only product. Its real significance is placement: it falls the day after BIGBANG at the National Stadium (17 Oct), so the 16-18 October weekend carries a stadium show and an arena show back to back and should be held as a firm two- to three-night block rather than treated as two separate one-nighters.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam - closest to Kallang, and the Bugis/Kampong Glam belt is where the regional K-pop travel segment concentrates for shopping and late-night food. City Hall second.

events.name: Singapore Night Festival 2026
events.attendees: Several hundred thousand across three weekends
events.rationale: Dates re-confirmed this run: the 17th edition runs 21 August to 5 September 2026 across the Bras Basah.Bugis precinct, spanning three weekends, themed around Singaporean and Southeast Asian myths and legends, with four festival hubs including a Museum Zone around the National Museum. Hours are 7.30pm to midnight Fridays and Saturdays, 7.30pm to 11pm on other nights, free entry with some ticketed programmes. Demand stays at Medium and is deliberately not higher: the audience is overwhelmingly local and day-trip, with families a large share, and free entry means it generates footfall rather than room nights. What justifies keeping it is duration and geography - sixteen consecutive nights of heavy evening activity directly adjacent to the Kampong Glam and City Hall sectors supports weekend leisure rates and gives a genuine reason-to-visit for the regional short-haul couple segment across three Fridays and Saturdays. Treat it as a rate-support and length-of-stay argument on weekends, not as a compression event.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam and City Hall - both sit inside or immediately on the edge of the Bras Basah.Bugis festival footprint, so guests walk to the installations rather than commute. This is the clearest walkability story of any event in the list for these two sectors.

events.name: Singapore Tennis Open 2026 (WTA 500)
events.attendees: ~3,000 capacity per session across a seven-day tournament
events.rationale: Re-confirmed this run and upgraded in status: the tournament returns 21-27 September 2026 at OCBC Arena as Southeast Asia's only WTA 500 event, with qualifying on 19-20 September, roughly US$1.2 million in prize money, a 28-player singles draw and 16-team doubles draw. The tier upgrade from WTA 250 matters because it attracts a stronger international field, and a stronger field means larger player entourages, more tour officials, more media and more sponsor hospitality - all of which are multi-night adult bookings rather than day admissions. The offsetting factor is scale: OCBC Arena seats only 3,000, and spectators are mostly local, so this is a Medium not a High. Its best feature is duration - seven main-draw days plus two qualifying days means nine consecutive nights of steady base demand for the tour-associated segment, and it overlaps Post Malone (25 Sep), MRO Asia-Pacific (22-24 Sep) and Submarine Networks World (23-24 Sep) to keep that whole week firm.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam - the Kallang Tennis Hub/OCBC Arena complex is closest to the Lavender/Nicoll Highway corridor, and touring players and officials prioritise short daily transfers over precinct character. City Hall second.

events.name: Avenged Sevenfold - Asia Tour 2026
events.rationale: Date re-confirmed this run on the Singapore Indoor Stadium listing: Tuesday 13 October 2026, no change and no cancellation. Metal audiences travel well within Southeast Asia and the demographic is solidly adult (30-45, groups and couples, few families), which fits an adults-only product, but a single midweek arena night keeps this at Medium. The placement is what earns its position: 13 October is the Tuesday immediately after the F1 weekend (9-11 Oct), so it catches the tail of race-week departures and gives a reason for a subset of guests to extend two extra nights rather than check out Monday morning. That extension effect is worth more than the show's own room generation. Manage it as a shoulder-support event on the Monday-Tuesday after F1 rather than pricing it as a peak.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam for Kallang proximity on a midweek 8pm start. City Hall second; note that F1 extenders will already be sitting in City Hall or The Quays and will simply stay put.

events.name: ITZY 3rd World Tour <TUNNEL VISION>
events.rationale: Date re-confirmed this run on the Singapore Indoor Stadium listing: Saturday 3 October 2026, unchanged. As a standalone event this is a Medium at best - a 12,000-seat fourth-generation K-pop show with a younger, more local and more price-sensitive audience than the BIGBANG or F✦FOREVER crowds, and a weaker fit for an adults-only property. Its value in this list is entirely about stacking: it falls on the same Saturday as the second Weeknd night at the National Stadium (2-3 Oct), which means roughly 67,000 concert admissions across two Kallang venues on one night, on the weekend immediately following SuperReturn Asia and Tech Week. That combination makes 3 October one of the two or three highest-compression single nights in the horizon. Price the night, not the event.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam for Kallang proximity. On this specific night, though, all four sectors will fill on the combined Weeknd/ITZY draw - the practical decision is to set a two-night minimum across the portfolio for 2-3 October rather than to differentiate by sector.

events.name: Power Station 'Life Goes On' World Tour
events.rationale: Date re-confirmed this run on the Singapore Indoor Stadium listing: Saturday 22 August 2026, unchanged and still on sale. Power Station are a long-running Taiwanese rock duo with a mature Mandopop following, so the audience is adult 40-60, couples and friend groups, with a meaningful Malaysian and Indonesian Chinese-speaking fly-in that treats a Singapore date as a weekend trip - a good profile for an adults-only product even if the absolute numbers are modest. Saturday placement is favourable and converts to two-night stays. It falls in the middle of the Singapore Night Festival (21 Aug-5 Sep) and one day into that festival's first weekend, and shares the week with the Asian Actuarial Conference (18-21 Aug) and ISPE Singapore (19-21 Aug), so the third week of August holds up better than a typical post-National-Day lull would suggest.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam for Kallang proximity and because the Mandopop weekend-trip segment gravitates to Bugis for shopping and supper after an arena show. City Hall second.

events.name: Sands Live Season - Jane Zhang (29 Aug) and Jonnie (30 Aug)
events.attendees: ~4,000 across two nights (Sands Theatre ~1,680 per night)
events.rationale: Re-confirmed this run against Marina Bay Sands' own Sands Live Season programming: Jane Zhang performs 29 August 2026 charting 21 years of classics, and Mandopop veteran Jonnie performs 30 August 2026 with his 'Looking Back, My Heart Remains' set. Two consecutive nights at Sands Theatre, capacity around 1,680, so the raw volume is small - this is a Medium on quality of guest rather than quantity. The Mandopop concert-tourism segment from Malaysia, Indonesia and Greater China is adult, couple-heavy, books a two- or three-night weekend around a marquee MBS show, and spends well on dining, which matches the property profile closely. Both nights fall on the Saturday-Sunday of a weekend that also carries Super 24 at the Indoor Stadium (29-30 Aug), and the Singapore Night Festival is running concurrently, so the end-of-August weekend is well supported despite being outside any major convention window.
events.best_fit: City Hall and The Quays for direct Bayfront access to Sands Theatre - a short walk or one MRT stop, which matters for a 10.30pm finish. Chinatown is a reasonable third for the rate-conscious end of this segment.

events.name: Sam Lee 'One Day' World Tour - Singapore
events.rationale: Re-confirmed this run on The Kallang's official event listing: Saturday 5 September 2026, 8pm, at the Singapore Indoor Stadium, following a Malaysian stop earlier in the year. Sam Lee (Li Sheng Jie) is a Taiwanese balladeer whose catalogue defined a generation, so the audience is adult 35-55 and heavily couple-oriented - a good demographic match - with cross-border ticket buying from Malaysia in particular given the tour routing. Medium rather than High because it is a single arena night with a large local Chinese-speaking base, so the incremental room generation is moderate. Placement is useful: it is the Saturday that closes out the Singapore Night Festival (which ends 5 September) and sits just before BEX Asia opens at Sands Expo (2-4 Sep, overlapping), giving the first weekend of September a firmer floor than it would otherwise have.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam for Kallang proximity and the Bugis supper circuit that this audience uses after a show. City Hall second.

events.name: 17th IHPBA World Congress 2026
events.attendees: ~2,000-3,000 international surgeons and clinicians
events.rationale: Dates and venue re-confirmed this run via the International Hepato-Pancreato-Biliary Association: the 17th World Congress runs 28-31 October 2026 at Suntec Singapore, with registration open. Medical world congresses are among the most reliable demand generators in the calendar - delegates are senior adult clinicians, almost entirely fly-in from Europe, North America, Japan, Korea, India and Australia, they register and book far in advance so materialisation risk is low, and a four-day scientific programme with pre-congress workshops produces genuine five-night stays. Held at Medium rather than High only because absolute headcount is in the low thousands rather than the tens of thousands. The important scheduling point this run is that it overlaps SIEW (26-30 Oct) almost completely, so the final week of October carries a 15,000-delegate energy summit at Marina Bay Sands and a multi-thousand-delegate surgical congress at Suntec simultaneously - that week should be at peak rate with no late discounting.
events.best_fit: City Hall is the clear first choice - Suntec is a covered walk from the City Hall/Esplanade/Promenade corridor, which matters for delegates carrying materials to early sessions. The Quays second; note that SIEW will be competing for the same City Hall inventory that week, so release Chinatown as the third option early.

events.name: LANY - soft world tour
events.rationale: Date re-confirmed this run on the Singapore Indoor Stadium listing: Wednesday 4 November 2026, unchanged. LANY have an exceptionally strong and durable Southeast Asian following and have sold out multiple Singapore runs previously, so materialisation history is good and the regional fly-in from the Philippines, Indonesia, Thailand and Malaysia is real. The audience is young-adult 20-35, couples and friend groups, no families - a workable if not ideal fit for an adults-only product. Medium because it is a single midweek arena night. Retained just past the three-month edge because it and My Chemical Romance (10-11 Nov) together mean early November is already firming, and the horizon decision that matters now is not to open November at soft shoulder rates on the assumption that demand collapses after SIEW ends on 30 October.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam for Kallang proximity on a midweek show. City Hall second.

events.name: Super 24 2026
events.attendees: ~12,000 per day; regional crews from 8+ countries
events.rationale: DOWNGRADED THIS RUN from Medium to Moderate. Dates re-confirmed on The Kallang's official listing for 29-30 August 2026 with crews from Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam, the Philippines, Thailand, Australia and China, and a published 29 August day pass covering tertiary finals, open qualifiers and open junior finals from 10am to about 10.30pm at S$28-S$68. The downgrade is on attendee type, not on the event's health: this is a day-pass format, the competitors are largely tertiary-student and junior dance crews, and the spectator base is local friends and families - precisely the profile the demand framework treats as low-value. Regional crews do fly in, but they travel as youth teams on tight budgets and book hostel or group accommodation, not adults-only aparthotel product. Kept in the list at Moderate only because it puts 12,000 people a day into Kallang across a weekend that also carries the Sands Live Season shows (29-30 Aug), which is worth knowing when reading citywide occupancy data for that weekend - but it should not drive rate.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam by geography (closest to Kallang), though realistically this event converts poorly for an adults-only product in any sector. Treat any Kampong Glam pickup that weekend as more likely driven by the Singapore Night Festival, which is running concurrently.

events.name: Firdhaus - Flat Earth Theory Concert Tour 2026
events.rationale: DOWNGRADED THIS RUN from Medium to Moderate. The date is re-confirmed on the Singapore Indoor Stadium listing for Saturday 12 September 2026 and the show is live and on sale, so this is not a viability concern. The downgrade is on attendee mix: Firdhaus is a homegrown Singaporean artist whose audience is predominantly local, with a Malaysian cross-border component but very little genuine long-haul or overnight fly-in demand. Under the framework that treats locals and day-attendees as low-value, a local-artist arena show generates footfall and F&B activity rather than room nights. Retained rather than dropped because a full 12,000-seat Saturday at the Indoor Stadium still tightens Kallang-adjacent supply and because a small regional Malay-language music-tourism segment does travel for it. Do not build rate strategy on this date; the second weekend of September is otherwise soft between BEX Asia (2-4 Sep) and the Tennis Open (21-27 Sep).
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam - both the closest sector to Kallang and the natural precinct for this artist's regional audience given the Malay-Muslim heritage district's dining and cultural draw. City Hall second.

events.name: Belle and Sebastian: If You're Feeling Sinister + Favourites
events.rationale: VENUE CORRECTED AND DOWNGRADED THIS RUN. The previous list had this at the Singapore Indoor Stadium; it is in fact at the Esplanade Concert Hall on 20 September 2026 at 7pm, ticketed through SISTIC, with the band performing 'If You're Feeling Sinister' in full for its 30th anniversary plus a second set of favourites. That is a capacity difference of roughly 12,000 versus 1,600, which changes the demand call entirely - hence the downgrade from Medium to Moderate. The audience quality is actually good for this property: indie-rock 30-year-anniversary shows draw an adult 35-55 crowd, and rare full-album performances do pull a genuine regional fly-in from Kuala Lumpur, Jakarta, Bangkok and Hong Kong because Singapore is the only Southeast Asian stop. But 1,600 seats caps the room impact at a few dozen nights. Useful as a Sunday-evening rate-support argument in the otherwise quiet run-up to the Tennis Open week, nothing more.
events.best_fit: City Hall - the Esplanade is a direct covered walk from the City Hall/Esplanade MRT corridor, which is the deciding factor for a 1,600-seat theatre audience that will not want a transfer. The Quays second via a short walk across the river.

events.name: 2026 Kit Chan Atrium Live Tour
events.rationale: Date re-confirmed this run on the Singapore Indoor Stadium listing: Saturday 19 September 2026, unchanged. Kit Chan is a Singaporean Mandopop institution, so the audience is adult 40-60 and couple-heavy, which suits an adults-only property, but it is overwhelmingly a home-market show with only a modest Malaysian and Indonesian cross-border draw - hence Moderate rather than Medium. Room generation is limited. Its practical value is timing: 19 September is the Saturday that opens the Singapore Tennis Open qualifying weekend (19-20 Sep) and sits three days before MRO Asia-Pacific (22-24 Sep) and Submarine Networks World (23-24 Sep) begin, so it marks the point where the second half of September starts to firm up after a soft first fortnight.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam for Kallang proximity, City Hall second. Given the largely local audience, expect minimal direct conversion in any sector - read this as a citywide-activity signal rather than a demand driver.

events.name: Singapore IP Week 2026
events.venue: Marina Bay Sands Expo & Convention Centre
events.attendees: ~1,500-2,000 IP professionals, policymakers and legal practitioners
events.rationale: Dates and venue re-confirmed this run on the official site: 26-27 August 2026 at Marina Bay Sands Expo and Convention Centre, organised by the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore, now in its 15th edition. Delegate quality is high - patent attorneys, IP counsel, WIPO and ASEAN IPA representatives, corporate innovation heads, almost all adult and corporate-funded - and the international share is meaningful given the FICPI and ASEAN IPA affiliations. What holds it at Moderate is scale and duration: two days and low thousands of delegates, with a substantial Singapore-resident legal-profession contingent who attend as day-attendees. Typical fly-in stay is two to three nights. It sits in the same week as the Sands Live Season shows (29-30 Aug) and inside the Singapore Night Festival run, contributing to a reasonably firm final week of August.
events.best_fit: City Hall and The Quays for Bayfront access to MBS. City Hall is preferred here because a large share of IP Week delegates also have meetings in the Raffles Place and Shenton Way legal corridor during the same trip.

events.name: ISPE Singapore Conference & Exhibition 2026
events.attendees: 2,600+ bio/pharma professionals from 30+ countries; 120+ exhibiting companies
events.rationale: Dates and venue re-confirmed this run via ISPE: 19-21 August 2026 at Suntec Singapore, themed 'Smart & Future-Ready Pharma: Global Vision, Local Agility', with an expanded showcase of 120+ exhibiting companies, an additional conference track on 20 August and two concurrent open-track programmes. The prior edition drew over 2,600 bio/pharma manufacturers and industry experts from more than 30 countries, which is a stronger international footprint than the Moderate rating implies - this is arguably a borderline Medium and should be watched for an upgrade next run if attendance guidance rises. Held at Moderate for now because Singapore's own large pharma-manufacturing workforce means a high local day-attendee share dilutes the room conversion. Fly-in delegates are adult, technical and corporate-funded, staying three nights. It runs concurrently with the Asian Actuarial Conference at MBS (18-21 Aug) and just after FLAsia and F✦FOREVER, making 13-21 August the densest sustained stretch of the month.
events.best_fit: City Hall - Suntec is directly connected via the Esplanade/Promenade covered walkway network, which is the practical differentiator for a three-day conference. The Quays second; Kampong Glam is a workable third via Bugis.

events.name: Asian Actuarial Conference 2026 (AAC26)
events.venue: Marina Bay Sands Expo & Convention Centre
events.attendees: 1,000+ delegates from across Asia
events.rationale: Dates and venue re-confirmed this run via the Singapore Actuarial Society: 18-21 August 2026 at Marina Bay Sands Expo and Convention Centre, themed 'Beating the Odds: Redefining Risk', with 1,000+ regional delegates, and held in conjunction with the Society's 50th anniversary including a gala dinner on 20 August. The anniversary framing is a positive signal for materialisation and for length of stay - anniversary editions reliably draw alumni and overseas members who would skip an ordinary year. Delegates are adult insurance and actuarial professionals from across Asia-Pacific with employer-funded travel, and a four-day programme supports genuine three- to four-night stays. Moderate rather than Medium purely on scale: 1,000 delegates with a significant Singapore-resident actuarial community attending as day-attendees limits the room block. Runs concurrently with ISPE at Suntec (19-21 Aug) and immediately after F✦FOREVER (14-16 Aug).
events.best_fit: City Hall and The Quays for Bayfront/MBS access. The Quays are worth pushing for the 20 August gala-dinner night, since the riverside is where delegate groups continue afterwards.

events.name: BEX Asia 2026 (The Built Environment Expo)
events.venue: Sands Expo & Convention Centre, Marina Bay Sands
events.attendees: 250+ global brands; several thousand built-environment professionals
events.rationale: Dates and venue re-confirmed this run: 2-4 September 2026 at Sands Expo & Convention Centre, bringing together over 250 global brands across green building, smart facility management and construction technology. Attendees are adult professionals - developers, architects, engineers, facility managers, sustainability consultants - but the visitor base is heavily Singapore and Malaysia-based, with day-attendance the norm and a modest genuine fly-in cohort concentrated among exhibitors and regional brand teams. That mix keeps it at Moderate. Exhibitor stands do generate three- to four-night stays including a build-up day. Its schedule value is that it is the only convention anchoring the otherwise thin first fortnight of September, overlapping the tail of the Singapore Night Festival and falling just before Sam Lee (5 Sep) - so the first week of September has a floor, but the second week (roughly 6-18 Sep) is the softest stretch of the entire horizon and is where promotional activity should be concentrated.
events.best_fit: City Hall and The Quays for Bayfront access. Chinatown is the practical third for exhibitor and contractor teams, who are the most rate-sensitive segment in this list and respond to a value CBD address.

events.name: Submarine Networks World 2026 (x Subsea Security World)
events.venue: Sands Expo & Convention Centre, Marina Bay Sands
events.attendees: 3,000+ senior executives from the global subsea community; 150+ speakers
events.rationale: Dates and venue re-confirmed this run via Terrapinn: 23-24 September 2026 at Marina Bay Sands Expo and Convention Centre, with 3,000+ senior executives from the global subsea community and 150+ speakers across seven theatres, including a new Subsea Security World theatre drawing government, navy, coastguard and policymaker attendees. The delegate profile is genuinely strong - almost entirely fly-in senior executives from cable operators, hyperscalers, carriers, marine contractors and now defence and government bodies, with no local day-attendee base to speak of. It is held at Moderate only because it is a compact two-day event, which caps stay length at two to three nights. NOTE FOR UPGRADE NEXT RUN: at 3,000+ senior international delegates this is close to Medium and the new government/defence theatre is likely to raise the international share further. It overlaps MRO Asia-Pacific at Singapore EXPO (22-24 Sep) and the Singapore Tennis Open (21-27 Sep) and precedes Post Malone (25 Sep), so the 21-27 September week is firm throughout.
events.best_fit: City Hall and The Quays for Bayfront access to Sands Expo. City Hall edges it for the government and defence delegates, who typically pair the conference with meetings in the civic and ministry district.

events.name: AOCR SGCR-WIRES 2026 (24th Asian Oceanian Congress of Radiology)
events.attendees: 1,000+ radiologists, interventional radiologists, nuclear medicine physicians, radiographers and industry partners
events.rationale: NEW THIS RUN - previously missing from the list, found on the Singapore EXPO events calendar and confirmed on the official congress site. The 24th Asian Oceanian Congress of Radiology, held jointly with SGCR-WIRES, runs 20-23 August 2026 at Singapore EXPO under the theme 'Imaging Beyond Borders, Shaping a Sustainable Future', bringing together over a thousand participants from across Asia-Oceania and beyond. Medical congress delegates are the most dependable segment in the calendar - senior adult clinicians, registered and booked well in advance, low cancellation risk, four-day programme supporting four- to five-night stays, and a strong industry-partner contingent that books separately. Rated Moderate rather than Medium on two counts: headcount is around a thousand rather than several thousand, and the Singapore EXPO location means a share of delegates default to Changi-side or East Coast hotels. It runs concurrently with ISPE at Suntec (19-21 Aug) and the Asian Actuarial Conference at MBS (18-21 Aug), so the third week of August carries three simultaneous international conferences - worth noting when reading that week's citywide data.
events.best_fit: Kampong Glam - Bugis offers a direct Downtown Line ride to Expo with no interchange, which is the deciding practical factor for a four-day congress with early daily starts. City Hall second via the East-West Line.
